answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with time-layered identity deposits, like sedimentary shale: new identities start with narrow privileges and gain more only after accumulating a public record of honest transactions. A swarm of fresh fakes shows no such strata, so peers can spot and throttle them. And just as a tidal inlet admits only so much water per cycle, established identities get a capped quota of vouches per epoch, so a rogue vouching for a tide of fakes exhausts its own quota first and honest work continues.
